questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Linear Transformation Represented by a Matrix
questions.problem: What linear transformation $T$ is represented by the matrix $T=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
Consider the standard basis ${i,j}$ of the Euclidean plane ${R}^{2}$ and the unit square spanned by the vectors, as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070817/assets/9e322e6ed1ddb8f1d094633e931cd179b7eb9d6f47acd7c7d0809f113df91b22.png)

Now, we compute the images of ${i,j}$ under $T$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =T(i)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=-j \\ {j}^{′} & =T(j)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=-i\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain the following image:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070817/assets/4a83673a409fd2e5d33b0b5f743f57af08cfb27c38e312a636179102c2172b04.png)

Therefore, the matrix represents a reflection in the line $y=-x.$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Linear Transformation Represented by a Matrix
questions.problem: What linear transformation $T$ is represented by the matrix $T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that a dilation of scale factor $k$ is represented by the matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}k & 0 \\ 0 & k\end{aligned}].
$$

Here, we have $k=2.$ Therefore, the matrix represents a dilation with a scale factor of $2.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Standard Matrix of a Dilation Given a Vector and its Image
questions.problem: A linear transformation $T$ represents a dilation.  Given that $v=[\begin{aligned}60 \\ 144\end{aligned}]$ and $T(v)=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 12\end{aligned}],$ what is the standard matrix of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
We can write $T(v)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}\cdot [\begin{aligned}60 \\ 144\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}v\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $T(v)=\frac{1}{12}v,$ and so the linear transformation $T$ is a dilation with scale factor $k=\frac{1}{12}.$

The matrix that represents a dilation of scale factor $k$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}k & 0 \\ 0 & k\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the standard matrix of $T$ is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{12} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{12}\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Linear Transformation Represented by a Matrix
questions.problem: What linear transformation $T$ is represented by the matrix $T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
Consider the standard basis ${i,j}$ of the Euclidean plane ${R}^{2}$ and the unit square spanned by the vectors, as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070817/assets/9e322e6ed1ddb8f1d094633e931cd179b7eb9d6f47acd7c7d0809f113df91b22.png)

Now, we compute the images of ${i,j}$ under $T$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =T(i)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=i \\ {j}^{′} & =T(j)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=-j\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain the following image:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070817/assets/dbe3773dea369f6b58fc2ad45a32f98c2c9ae356701baf3ab56af3daa6ca732d.png)

Therefore, the matrix represents a reflection across the $x$-axis.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Standard Matrix of a Dilation Given a Vector and its Image
questions.problem:
A  linear transformation $T$ represents a dilation. Given that $v=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -9\end{aligned}]$ and $T(v)=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -15\end{aligned}],$ what is the standard matrix $T$ of $T?$

| $T=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
We can write $T(v)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -15\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{5}{3}\cdot [\begin{aligned}6 \\ -9\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{5}{3}v\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $T(v)=\frac{5}{3}v,$ and so the linear transformation $T$ is a dilation with scale factor $k=\frac{5}{3}.$

The matrix that represents a dilation of scale factor $k$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}k & 0 \\ 0 & k\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the standard matrix of $T$ is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}].
$$
